concepts.why: The patient has a low hemoglobin level of 9.65 g/dL, indicating anemia.
The patient has a history of prosthetic mitral valve thrombosis and is experiencing symptoms of dyspnea on exertion and orthopnea.
The patient has an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein, indicating an inflammatory response.
The patient has an elevated prothrombin time and INR, indicating a coagulopathy.
The patient has a history of rheumatic mitral stenosis and is experiencing symptoms of dyspnea on exertion and orthopnea.
The patient received streptokinase two weeks prior to presentation and is now experiencing fever and bilateral knee pain, suggesting an inflammatory response to the treatment.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient presents with fever, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and positive C-reactive protein, which are all indicative of an inflammatory response. Additionally, the patient's symptoms of bilateral knee pain and recent administration of streptokinase support this diagnosis. Coagulopathy is also a strong consideration due to the patient's prolonged prothrombin time and elevated INR, but the inflammatory response better explains the patient's overall clinical presentation.
